title: Service stability collab playfest - Q1 2027
content:
Purpose and context:
This doc is a lightweight, cross-functional campaign plan to align engineering, product, platform, and customer success on a focused stability push for model-serving surfaces in Q1 2027. Working name: 'Playfest' — short, timeboxed, lots of pairing, experiments, and concrete outcomes rather than long proposals.

High-level objectives (measurable):
- Reduce p95 tail latency for hosted API text generation by 30% under the nominal traffic mix within the quarter (baseline: 310ms p95).
- Reduce production error rate for streaming responses by 50% (baseline: 0.8% tpm).
- Ensure 100% of top-5 customer flows have explicit SLO owners, alerts, and escalation contacts.
- Produce a repeatable SLO adoption checklist and a templated canary policy for model rollouts.

Scope (what we will and won’t do):
- In-scope: hosted-api text generation, streaming pipeline, routing policies, and observability dashboards for top-5 services. Also: onboarding docs for SLO ownership and a canary recipe.
- Out-of-scope: dedicated/private deployment orchestration changes, quantization-level runtime tuning, or infra procurement. Those will be handed off to respective teams with clear acceptance criteria.

Approach and cadence:
- Timebox: 8 weeks (kickoff week + 6 experimental sprints + wrap-up week).
- Weekly rhythm: Mon sync (30m cross-team), Wed drop-in pairing (ad-hoc pairing slots, 2x2-hour windows), Fri outcomes (30m demo + decisions).
- Work style: pairing-first (SREs pair with feature owners), follow-the-metric experiments, quick hypothesis->test->rollback pattern.

Roles and RACI (working):
- Campaign lead: Priya Menon (SRE) — overall schedule, decisions, triage.
- Product liaison: Lucas Rivera — stakes, customers, acceptance criteria.
- Observability lead: Ethan Zhao — dashboards, SLI definitions, instrumentation backlog.
- Platform contact: Harper Nguyen — routing/capacity changes, canary infra.
- CS/Customer voice: Sofia Alvarez — customer impact, contact prioritization.
- Exec sponsor: Noah Bennett — escalation and resource unblock.

Deliverables (granular):
1) SLI/SLO pack for each top-5 flow: one-pager with SLI definition, measurement query (PromQL/SQL), SLO target, owner, alert thresholds, and runbook link.
2) Canary rollout recipe: step-by-step script, traffic split plan, success criteria, automated rollback hook.
3) Telemetry gap list: prioritized list of missing metrics/traces with owners and ETA.
4) Stability experiments log: experiment hypothesis, test plan, result, decision, and next action.
5) Postmortem-lite template for transient degradations encountered during tests.
6) Adoption checklist and SLO onboarding doc for feature teams.

Milestones and week-by-week plan:
- Week 0 (kickoff): align goals, select top-5 flows, baseline collection, set up skeleton dashboards, communicate schedule to stakeholders.
- Weeks 1–3 (experimentation phase A): two concurrent experiments per flow (latency mitigation & error reduction). Track p50/p95/p99, error counts, throughput.
- Week 4 (midpoint retro): review experiments, triage failures, adjust hypotheses.
- Weeks 5–6 (experimentation phase B): iterate on successful signals, expand canary recipes to additional routing policies.
- Week 7 (wrap & docs): finalize SLI packs, publish onboarding checklist, handoff for production rollouts.

Instrumentation and telemetry requirements (practical):
- Must have a stable p95 metric per flow (PromQL query example included below).
- Tagging conventions: route_id, model_variant, customer_tier, region. Ensure logs and traces include these fields.
- Sampling policy for traces during high load: 1% baseline + 100% for errors > threshold.
- Default dashboard template: p50/p95/p99, request rate, errors, queue depth, GPU util, KV cache hit rate.

Example SLI definition (note to implementers):
- Name: text-gen-hosted.p95.latency
- Query: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le, route_id)) by (route_id)
- Window: 5-minute rolling, aggregated hourly for SLO burn calculations.

Rollout and canary policy (template):
- Step 0: baseline validation (10m): verify telemetry ingestion and dashboards.
- Step 1: 1% traffic for 30m. If p95 <= target and errors stable -> proceed.
- Step 2: 5% for 30m. Repeat checks.
- Step 3: 25% for 30m. If step fails, automated rollback to previous variant and open incident (owner notified).
- Post-rollout: 72-hour watch window with elevated trace sampling and daily review.

Success criteria and acceptance:
- Experiment success: pre-defined hypothesis confirmed with statistically significant improvement or clear learning and next steps.
- SLO acceptance: service owners sign-off on SLI definition and alerting.
- Canary acceptance: no regressions in 72 hours and no increase in customer-facing errors.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: experiments cause customer-visible regressions. Mitigation: start with internal traffic or low-risk customers, enforce strict rollback automation.
- Risk: telemetry gap prevents accurate measurement. Mitigation: small precursor task in Week 0 to ensure baseline metrics are present; experiments paused until resolved.
- Risk: resource contention (platform capacity). Mitigation: coordinate with platform early; reserve canary capacity windows.

Open questions / decision backlog (to resolve at kickoff):
- Final list of top-5 flows — product to confirm by D+3.
- Agreement on canonical p95 measurement (histogram vs summary).
- Canary automation ownership: platform or SRE? Proposal: platform owns infra; SRE owns policy and rollback logic.

Communication channels and artifacts:
- Slack channel: #sre-playfest-q1-2027 (create on kickoff).
- Weekly notes: short outcomes and decisions posted to Confluence page linked above.
- Demo day: public demo to eng and product at the end of campaign.

Checklist / immediate next steps (before kickoff):
- [ ] Product to confirm top-5 flows (Lucas) — due 2026-12-03.
- [ ] Platform to provision canary capacity windows (Harper) — due 2026-12-10.
- [ ] Observability to populate baseline dashboards (Ethan) — due 2026-12-15.
- [ ] CS to prioritize customer flows and provide contact list (Sofia) — due 2026-12-08.
- [ ] Exec sponsor to confirm resource allocation (Noah) — due 2026-12-01.

Notes to self / informal thoughts:
- Keep experiments low-friction: small feature flags, short TTLs.
- Emphasize pairing — it accelerates knowledge transfer and surfaces runbook gaps early.
- After the playfest, we should have 80% of the artifacts be templates that other teams can reuse.

Meeting prep for kickoff:
- 15-minute demo of the baseline dashboards (Ethan).
- Quick readout from product: why these flows matter to customers (Lucas).
- Platform primer on canary infra (Harper).
- Confirm owners and sign the RACI in the kickoff doc.

Appendix: useful snippets and links (working):
- PromQL p95 example: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(api_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route_id))
- Suggested alert thresholds: p95 > 1.4x target for 15m -> P1 alert; error rate > 2x baseline for 10m -> P1.
- Canaries: prefer traffic-splitper v2 API (see linked PR).

If you have edits or want to pair on a specific flow, drop a note in the doc or ping me in the Slack channel. This is intentionally lightweight — the goal is to learn fast and leave behind reusable artifacts.

-- Priya
